answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, escrowed trades with distinct counterparties, and each trade counts only after the counterparty risks a deposit too. A graph-based rule discounts clusters whose members transact mainly with one another, so an attacker cannot cheaply mint identities and circulate tokens to manufacture trust. To gain weight, the attacker must fund many independent deposits and sustain costly, externally verifiable exchanges; walnut, timber, and basalt are merely labels, not shortcuts around that requirement.
